description: Start a life sciences investigation in your AI assistant. Find evidence, work with data and models, and run computational experiments with your approval. Biosimulant keeps the setup, results, and research notes together in Studio so you can check what happened, rerun it, or pick up where you left off.

defaultPrompt: Pick up my protein-binding study. What have we tried, and what is still open?
Prepare a rerun with the saved settings and show me the cost.
Compare two completed runs and tell me what the saved outputs support.

positive.description: Discover and inspect an exact published human-physiology lab
positive.prompt: Find the published Guyton stress-relaxation lab and explain what it simulates and its important limitations. Do not run or change anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds and inspects demi/guyton1972-stress-relaxation@1.1.0, a public human-physiology lab. Explains short- and long-term venous stress relaxation after a normalized-volume change, built-in inputs and source clock. States that it is an isolated subsystem, does not predict blood pressure or patient outcomes, and is not biologically validated or runtime-qualified merely because it is published. No changes or compute.

positive.description: Find and save a life sciences source record
positive.prompt: Search PubMed for Michaelis–Menten kinetics and save the exact source record for PMID 42759140. Explain what was saved and its limitations; do not attach it to a lab.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds and stores the exact PubMed citation record with its source identifier, retrieval provenance, checksum and citation-only reuse rule. Explains that saving a source record does not validate its claims or establish that it is the best general reference. No lab changes or simulation. If a source is unavailable, report that honestly without substituting evidence.

positive.prompt: Draft requirements for an exploratory Michaelis–Menten enzyme model. Assume a single substrate, constant enzyme concentration, and no inhibition. I have no experimental validation data. Identify what evidence and tests are missing.
positive.tools_triggered: build-or-adapt-a-model skill; no MCP write or run is required
positive.expected_behavior: Produces a requirements draft separating user assumptions from evidence, with intended use, inputs/outputs and units to resolve, measurable acceptance criteria, missing validation data and non-use limitations. Does not invent measurements, imply clinical validity or claim the draft is saved in Biosimulant without a successful explicit write.

positive.description: Copy a public physiology lab and prepare an approval-bound simulation
positive.prompt: Copy demi/guyton1972-stress-relaxation@1.1.0 into a new private lab named Reviewer physiology test. Prepare a Modal simulation using its defaults with a 120-second wall-clock limit. Show the exact plan, inputs, limitations and cost before running it. Do not execute or publish anything.
positive.tools_triggered: hub_inspect, workspace_create, run_prepare; run_create only after separate exact-plan approval
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a private lab and immutable revision from the exact public release. Preserves defaults and scientific limitations. Returns the actual plan fingerprint, workspace/revision, Modal provider, inputs/parameters, 120-second wall-clock limit, costs, expiry and any blockers. Stops before execution. Only after separate explicit approval of that current exact plan may it execute once and retain the run reference for case 5. Expired or changed plans require new approval. No publication. A blocked plan must not be reported as a successful preparation.

positive.description: Retrieve saved scientific results and explain evidence limitations
positive.prompt: For the run created in the previous test, check its outcome, retrieve the actual saved results and evidence report, and explain what they establish in plain English. Do not start another run or publish anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Uses the exact previous run reference and reports execution success only from terminal status. Retrieves actual saved scientific output: either full bytes with independently checked size/SHA-256, or bounded JSON values after the server verifies the full artifact size/SHA-256. A preview must identify exact paths/array indices, disclose sampling and omissions, and must not be described as an independent client checksum calculation or full download. Metadata alone is not sufficient. Explains the signed Passport decision and scientific limitations. Distinguishes sample averages from final values. Successful execution or READY does not establish biological or clinical validation. If actual saved values cannot be retrieved, report the failure honestly; do not invent them.

negative.description: General biology explanation without a request for sources, stored work or simulation; answer directly without calling Biosimulant.
negative.prompt: Explain the difference between DNA and RNA in simple terms.

negative.description: A request for medical diagnosis or personalized treatment; Biosimulant is a research tool and must not be used to diagnose or prescribe.
negative.prompt: Use my symptoms to diagnose my illness and tell me which prescription dose to take.
